Project overview
About sRNA-TAPS
sRNA-TAPS is an open-source analysis pipeline developed in the Schneider Lab at the Institute of Chemical Epigenetics Munich (ICEM), LMU Munich. It adapts TET-assisted pyridine borane sequencing (TAPS) to study cytosine modifications in small RNA, where short, repetitive, and strand-specific molecules create distinct analytical challenges.
Built specifically for small-RNA data, the workflow combines TAPS-aware alignment, single-locus read assignment, biotype-resolved modification calling, and a three-condition framework for chemistry-based background correction. It supports analysis of m5C and hm5C across miRNA, tRNA, rRNA, snoRNA, snRNA, piRNA, and lncRNA with species-aware reference support, without the harsh degradation associated with bisulfite treatment.
Designed for
Small-RNA complexity
TAPS-aware alignment is adapted to short, repetitive, and strand-specific molecules.
Built around
Reliable signal correction
A three-condition framework separates modification signal from chemistry background from the start.
Covers
Multiple RNA biotypes
Modification calling is resolved across miRNA, tRNA, rRNA, snoRNA, snRNA, piRNA, and lncRNA.

What matters

Readout

Framing
Why existing tools fall short for small RNA
Most methylation callers were designed for DNA or for long, abundant RNA species. Applying them to small RNA introduces three systematic problems:
rastair
DNA-oriented
Designed for TAPS data but optimised for DNA methylation calling. Lacks biotype-aware splitting and uses fixed coverage thresholds inappropriate for short RNA species.
asTair
RNA-compatible
Supports RNA TAPS but does not distinguish between RNA biotypes. Applies uniform calling parameters across miRNA, tRNA, and rRNA — which have fundamentally different coverage profiles and multi-mapping characteristics.
Bismark
Bisulfite
Built for bisulfite sequencing where unmodified C converts to T. The signal direction is inverted relative to TAPS — modified C stays as C in bisulfite but converts to T in TAPS. Bismark results must be inverted for comparison.

What sequencing depth do I need for reliable m5C detection?
↓
Per-sample coverage thresholds vary by biotype: rRNA requires ≥10x, miRNA, tRNA and snoRNA ≥3x, and snRNA, piRNA, lncRNA and other biotypes ≥5x. Replicate-level testing uses coverage of at least 5. In practice, deeper coverage improves sensitivity and reduces false positives. For miRNA, we recommend at least 20–30x coverage at expressed loci. Standard small RNA-seq libraries of 10–20 million reads per sample are generally sufficient.
Can I use sRNA-TAPS without a pb_Ctrl condition?
↓
No. The condition module expects treatment, pb_Ctrl and untreated samples. Sites are called against the untreated control, and pb_Ctrl quantifies PB-associated background so that a corrected modification level can be reported. Use at least three replicates per condition.
Why are most of my reads assigned to the "other" biotype?
↓
The "other" category captures reads that do not overlap a uniquely annotated Ensembl feature, or that map to regions where multiple biotypes share equal priority in the annotation hierarchy. This is common in small RNA-seq data and does not indicate a pipeline problem.
Several factors can contribute to a high "other" fraction: reads mapping to unannotated intergenic regions, reads overlapping antisense transcripts or pseudogenes not classified under the main biotypes, and multi-mapping reads that cannot be confidently assigned to a single locus. In TAPS-treated samples,

reads overlapping antisense transcripts or pseudogenes not classified under the main biotypes, and multi-mapping reads that cannot be confidently assigned to a single locus. In TAPS-treated samples, the chemical conversion step can also affect alignment scores at modified positions, occasionally pushing reads into ambiguous mapping territory.
To reduce the "other" fraction, ensure you are using a current Ensembl GTF for your selected species and release, that your alignment is to the full genome rather than a transcriptome, and that your GTF biotype priority list covers the RNA species most relevant to your experiment.
My alignment rate is very low — what should I check?
↓
First check that adapter trimming ran correctly — untrimmed reads align poorly. Confirm that alignment.strategy is three_letter. If your alignment rate is below 60%, check the trimming report for adapter content and read length distribution. For synthetic test data, ~80% alignment is expected; for real data, 70–90% is typical depending on library quality.
Can I run sRNA-TAPS on mouse or other non-human genomes?
↓
Yes. sRNA-TAPS now supports species-aware reference setup, with built-in Ensembl-backed configurations for human, mouse, rat, zebrafish, fruit fly, c_elegans, and chicken, plus custom FASTA/GTF inputs for other organisms. For non-human runs, use the matching genome FASTA, annotation, and any species-appropriate variant resources you need for filtering.

A negative δ means the control rate is higher than the treatment rate at that position. This can reflect a sequence variant or a position with unusual background reactivity. Such a site does not meet the minimum difference of 0.10 and is not called.

↓

Stage 07a: Sample-profile QC
Stage 07a uses the raw, per-sample calls from stage 07 to inspect sample-level modification profiles before pooling and statistical filtering. It provides an early QC view of experimental structure, local neighbours, and unusual replicates.
The default three-condition UMAP uses the Aurora condition palette: PB- TET-, PB+ TET-, and PB+ TET+. Cell line is shown by point shape. DBSCAN membership, outliers, neighbours, and statistical tests are saved as tables instead of being printed on the figure.
For the direct PB+ TET- versus PB+ TET+ comparison, the pipeline also provides PCA with explained-variance axes. PCA is deterministic and is the preferred presentation for this focused two-group comparison. A four-of-six replicate centroid-proximity sensitivity analysis is available for QC only; it does not replace the prespecified six-replicate analysis.

Tools: wget, samtools faidx, bowtie-build
Species-aware references: The default registry includes human, mouse, rat, zebrafish, fruit fly, c_elegans, and chicken. Human still defaults to GRCh38, but any supported species can be selected through reference.species.

If the genome FASTA or GTF do not exist at the paths in config.yaml, the pipeline derives them from reference.species and downloads the matching Ensembl release automatically. The Ensembl release is set by ensembl_release in config (default: 112). The unmasked dna.toplevel FASTA is always used — the repeat-masked version soft-masks cytosines, which would suppress genuine C→T TAPS modification signal.
If your genome files already exist on disk, all download and indexing steps are skipped. The Bowtie1 index is built once from the FASTA and reused for all samples.
Existing index: Point genome_fa, gtf, and bowtie1_index in config.yaml to your existing files. Snakemake will skip download automatically.
Step 1 — Quality Control
Tool: FastQC, MultiQC
FastQC runs on raw FASTQs before trimming and on trimmed FASTQs after. MultiQC aggregates all results — FastQC, Trim Galore reports, and Bowtie1 alignment logs — into a single interactive HTML report at report/multiqc_report.html. For small RNA libraries, expect a dominant length peak at 18–22 nt (miRNA) and a second peak at 26–32 nt (tRNA fragments and piRNAs). All reads will contain adapter sequence since small RNA inserts are shorter than the read length.
Step 2 — Adapter Trimming
Tool: Trim Galore (Cutadapt)
Trim Galore removes the TruSeq small RNA 3′ adapter (TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG) and quality-trims the 3′ end. Reads shorter than 18 nt are discarded. The --small_rna flag sets sensible defaults for this library type.

Step 3 — TAPS-aware Alignment
Tool: Bowtie 1.3.1, SAMtools
Alignment is to the whole reference genome rather than a transcriptome — tRNA families (~600 gene copies), piRNA clusters, and snoRNA loci need genomic coordinates for correct downstream annotation. Three-letter alignment neutralises TAPS conversions during mapping:

Single-locus assignmentEach read is reported at one locus (-k 1), so reads from repetitive or paralogous loci go to one representative locus
Sequence restorationOriginal bases and qualities are restored before modification calling

Tool: Custom Python script (pysam), Ensembl GTF for the configured species
Reads are assigned to the highest-priority overlapping biotype using the Ensembl GTF, and separate sorted BAMs are written per biotype per sample:
miRNA > tRNA > piRNA > snoRNA > snRNA > rRNA > lncRNA > other
A biotype composition summary (05.biotype_bams/*_biotype_summary.txt) is written alongside each BAM for downstream QC figures.

For each cytosine position with sufficient coverage:
mod_rate = T_count / (C_count + T_count)

Strand-specific logicForward strand: modified C reads as T. Reverse strand: modified C reads as A.
CIGAR-aware parsingget_aligned_pairs() handles indels and soft-clipping without positional offsets

Tool: Custom Python
Pooled contrast. Counts are pooled within each condition. For sites with coverage of at least 5 in treatment and both controls, treatment is compared with each control using a one-sided Fisher's exact test with BH correction. This tier does not gate the replicate model.

Replicate model. With at least 3 replicates per condition, each rate has the posterior Beta(1 + total modified, 1 + total unmodified). A site is called against the untreated control when the posterior probability of a difference of at least 0.10 is at least 0.95, and the median-of-replicates difference is also at least 0.10. The same difference against pb_Ctrl quantifies PB-associated background and is not a pass/fail gate.

Tutorial
A complete walkthrough using the 100-sample synthetic test dataset included with sRNA-TAPS. By the end you will have run the full Snakemake pipeline from raw FASTQs to called m5C sites, automatic R report figures, and, optionally, a three-tool benchmarking comparison.

Verify expected signal

Before you start: You need a SLURM cluster with the sRNA-TAPS conda environment active, R packages installed (Rscript install_R_packages.R), and the sRNA-TAPS repository cloned. No pre-built genome index is required — the pipeline downloads the configured species reference automatically.
1
Generate the test FASTQs
The simulator generates 100 samples with accurate TAPS chemistry — seeded m5C positions at 60 to 90% conversion in treat and 1 to 3% background in no-treat. Reads are 18–50 nt with the TruSeq small RNA adapter, drawn from real hg38 loci (miRNA 40%, tRNA 25%, rRNA 25%, snoRNA 10%).

chunks.title: Carissimi et al. (2021): human miRNA (h)m5C mapping
chunks.text: BS-miRNA-seq and MAmBA map cytosine modifications in human miRNAs. Bisulfite non-conversion does not by itself distinguish m5C from hm5C. The project curated position-resolved mature-miRNA records; use each atlas record's matching mature arm, nucleotide position and source table rather than assigning this paper to every site in a miRNA family. Antibody validation supports both modifications in mature miRNAs, not automatic chemical identification of every individual called site.

chunks.title: Konno et al. (2019): mature miRNAs in gastrointestinal cancer
chunks.text: The project's curated master records targeted MALDI-TOF-MS/MS evidence for miR-200c-3p mature C9 and miR-21-5p mature C9. These are specific miRNA/site records, not evidence that all cytosines or both arms are methylated. Interpret tissue, serum and disease observations in the study's sample context. The curated notes flag a miR-21 arm-label inconsistency in the article text; the supplementary MS/MS evidence identifies 5p.

chunks.title: Cheray et al. (2020): miRNA methylation in glioblastoma
chunks.text: The curated project records distinguish exact mature-nucleotide evidence, candidate CpG position sets from small-RNA bisulfite sequencing, and nonpositional anti-m5C immunoprecipitation array enrichment. A miRNA-level array result is not proof of a particular C position. Candidate CpG summaries from three U87 replicates must not be reported as independently measured methylation rates for every candidate nucleotide. Preserve the resolution attached to each source record.

chunks.title: Ohshiro et al. (2021): single-molecule RNA modification detection
chunks.text: Single-molecule RNA sequencing was investigated for simultaneous detection of m6A and 5mC. The project's curated master includes five exact mature-nucleotide records from this study. Consult an exact matched atlas citation before claiming a particular miRNA position; do not extrapolate a demonstrated method to all small RNAs.

chunks.title: Lü et al. (2024): purified mature-miRNA LC-MS/MS
chunks.text: Two-step hybridization purification was coupled to LC-MS/MS to measure modifications in mature miRNAs. The project's curated records classify this evidence as miRNA-level and nonpositional. Modified nucleoside abundance in purified RNA does not alone identify a modified nucleotide coordinate.

chunks.title: Zeng et al.: miRNAs in minimal change disease
chunks.text: The project's curated master includes 83 miRNA-level, nonpositional records under this publication, labeled 2026 in the local bibliography (PMID 41235950). Use the source publication for publication-date details. These records are not exact nucleotide validation and cannot establish that an arbitrary atlas C site was previously reported. This entry is a pointer to the locally curated literature, not an independently revalidated site map.

chunks.title: Haag et al. (2015): NSUN6 and tRNA C72
chunks.text: Human NSUN6 methylates C72 in specific tRNA-Cys and tRNA-Thr substrates. Recognition depends on the 3-prime CCA tail in the reported in-vitro experiments. This finding should not be generalized to every tRNA with cytosine at that coordinate. Use mature-tRNA numbering and species-specific substrate identity.

chunks.title: NSUN2-dependent methylation and tRNA fragmentation (2014)
chunks.text: Loss of NSUN2-dependent cytosine methylation increased angiogenin-mediated tRNA cleavage and accumulation of 5-prime tRNA fragments in the studied human and mouse systems, with effects on translation and cellular stress. Modification on a parental tRNA and detection in a tRNA-derived fragment are related but distinct observations. Do not infer a causal cleavage mechanism from one atlas call alone.

chunks.title: Human DNMT2 and tRNA-Asp C38 (2008)
chunks.text: Human DNMT2 catalyzes methylation of C38 in tRNA-Asp using a DNA-methyltransferase-like catalytic mechanism. DNMT2 is also known as TRDMT1. Cite substrate-specific experiments; this evidence does not assign DNMT2 as the writer for all small-RNA m5C sites.

chunks.title: NSUN3 and ALKBH1: mitochondrial tRNA-Met modification pathway (2016)
chunks.text: NSUN3 introduces m5C34 in mitochondrial tRNA-Met and ALKBH1/ABH1 oxidizes it to f5C34, expanding codon recognition. A signal at this coordinate must be interpreted with the assay's chemical specificity: pathway involvement does not prove the endpoint is unoxidized m5C. Distinguish mitochondrial tRNA-Met from cytoplasmic tRNA-Met.

chunks.title: NSUN5 and ribosomal RNA methylation (2019)
chunks.text: NSUN5 introduces m5C at human 28S rRNA C3782 and mouse 28S rRNA C3438 in the reported study. The species and reference numbering matter. A short RNA read assigned to rRNA may derive from a large rRNA precursor; do not classify the intact 28S molecule as a small RNA or transfer a coordinate between species without mapping.

chunks.title: TAPS chemistry: original DNA method (2019)
chunks.text: The original DNA TAPS method uses TET oxidation of 5mC/5hmC to 5caC and pyridine-borane reduction to dihydrouracil, producing C-to-T readout. It is a DNA study, not experimental validation of the project's RNA adaptation. Treat the sRNA-TAPS documentation as the source for its RNA workflow and controls; do not equate the two validation scopes.

chunks.title: Pyridine-borane readout and RNA oxidation products (2022)
chunks.text: Reactivity-dependent profiling of RNA 5-methylcytidine dioxygenases investigated RNA oxidation products and pyridine-borane-based readout, including mitochondrial tRNA-Met. Native oxidized cytosines can matter for interpretation of a conversion signal. Use the actual treatment and control scheme rather than labeling every C-to-T event as chemically specific m5C.
